Amittai
uh-MIT-eye
n. (the father of the prophet Jonah)
Hebrew Amittay (H573), truthful, from emeth, truth, faithfulness.

Biblical Definition

Amittai is known to Scripture solely as the father of one of its most memorable prophets, named at the opening of both books that record his son’s ministry: “now the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying” (Jonah 1:1), and again in the historical notice of Jonah’s earlier, successful prophetic word to Israel — “he restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the LORD God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gathhepher” (2 Kings 14:25). This second reference is historically significant: it confirms Jonah as a real, datable prophet active in the northern kingdom under Jeroboam II, whose message of territorial restoration actually came to pass, establishing his credentials before the more famous and more reluctant commission to Nineveh recorded in his own book. That commission came not once but twice: “the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time, saying” (Jonah 3:1), after Jonah’s flight and the great fish, repeating the original charge — “arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me” (Jonah 1:2). Amittai’s own name, meaning truthful, stands in quiet tension with his son’s recorded flight from the LORD’s truth-bearing errand, a tension the book of Jonah never resolves except in Jonah’s own eventual, reluctant obedience.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Amittai; his name means truthful, and Scripture knows him only as the father of the prophet Jonah, named in both 2 Kings and the book of Jonah.

expand to see more

AMITTAI, n. The father of the prophet Jonah, named in 2 Kings 14:25 and Jonah 1:1.

JONAH, n. A prophet of Israel under Jeroboam II, sent to pronounce judgment on Nineveh, remembered for fleeing his commission and being swallowed by a great fish.

PROPHET, n. One who speaks by divine inspiration; one who foretells future events or declares the will of God.

NINEVEH, n. The ancient capital of Assyria, the object of Jonah's reluctant preaching and subsequent repentance.

COMMISSION, n. A charge, warrant, or authority given to a person to act on another's behalf; in Scripture, a divine calling to a task.

Key Scripture

Jonah 1:1 — "Now the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,"

2 Kings 14:25 — "He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the LORD God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gathhepher."

Jonah 3:1 — "And the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time, saying,"

Jonah 1:2 — "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me."

Modern Corruption

An incidental historical cross-reference in 2 Kings confirming the prophet named in Jonah's own book, complete with hometown and reigning king, is the kind of unforced corroboration a late, fictionalized parable would not bother to plant.

expand to see more

Critical readings that treat the book of Jonah as pure parable or late didactic fiction with no historical prophet behind it have to explain away 2 Kings 14:25's matter-of-fact historical notice, written in a wholly different genre and context, naming the same prophet, the same father, and even his hometown of Gath-hepher — an independent historical anchor a deliberately fictional composition gains nothing by including and every reason to omit if inventing the figure from nothing.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD's word, given twice to the son of a man named Truthful, does not change between the first commission and the second — the repeated charge to Nineveh in Jonah 3:1 is identical in substance to the first in Jonah 1:2, a reminder that flight from a divine calling delays but does not alter what the LORD has determined to do, and that His patience in repeating the call is itself a mercy to the reluctant messenger, not only to the city awaiting the message.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Amittay (H573), from emeth (H571), truth, faithfulness; nabi' (H5030), prophet; dabar (H1697), word; shuv (H7725), to turn, return, repent.

expand to see more

Hebrew Amittay (H573) — truthful, from emeth, truth, faithfulness.

Hebrew emeth (H571) — truth, faithfulness; the root of Amittai's own name.

Hebrew nabi' (H5030) — prophet; the office Amittai's son Jonah held.

Hebrew dabar (H1697) — word; what came to Jonah, twice, from the LORD.

Hebrew shuv (H7725) — to turn, return, repent; the verb governing both Jonah's own flight and Nineveh's eventual repentance.

Usage

"“The word of the LORD came unto Jonah the son of Amittai” — the opening of his son's book."

"“Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gathhepher” — the historical confirmation in 2 Kings."

"“The word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time” — the renewed commission after his flight."
